recipes.name: Greenmend Salve
recipes.description: A cool, clean salve tuned for wilted planter beds and delicate specimens.
recipes.lore_note: The glasshouse still rewards purity above force.

recipes.name: Hollowroot Revival
recipes.description: A dead cutting and living pollen. The still does not brew this so much as ask the specimen whether it would like to try again.
recipes.lore_note: It cannot be done without pollen from a bloomwing, which is exactly why the plant died: nothing was carrying for it.

discovery_milestones.title: It Came Back
discovery_milestones.text: A plant the valley finished losing twenty years ago, growing out of a cutting and a guess. Rowan asked to be shown the bench three times and then stopped asking and just came up.

recipes.name: Hollowroot Cordial
recipes.description: The first thing brewed from a plant the valley had already finished losing.
recipes.lore_note: Mira asked what it tasted like. Ione said 'like a page' and would not be drawn further.

recipes.name: Terracemend Salve
recipes.description: Made from what grows on the tower's own walls. Brin uses it on ground that has been let go rather than ground that has been worked wrong.
recipes.lore_note: The terraces produce the thing that repairs terraces, which Brin says is either very good design or a joke at his expense.

recipes.name: Southmarket Salve
recipes.description: Imported resin cut with something that grows on burnt wood ten minutes up the road. Mira says the valley has been paying for half of this unnecessarily for years.
recipes.lore_note: Two to a batch, which is the only reason anybody can justify the myrrh.

recipes.name: Farcarried Tonic
recipes.description: The plant and the seed it throws, brewed together for the first time. Rowan wanted it on record that she had asked where the seed came from for nine years.
recipes.lore_note: Half of this walked down into the valley on the wind and half of it had to be walked up to.

recipes.name: Leanaway Salve
recipes.description: Cushion plant off the windward stone, worked down with moss. It does not close a wound quickly. It stops the wound getting any worse while somebody walks four hours on it.
recipes.lore_note: Tarn carries it and Wren stocks it, and the two of them arrived at that independently before either knew the other had.

recipes.name: Underglass Tonic
recipes.description: The cushion that survives the wind by lying under it and the bell that will not open in valley air, in the same pot for the first time. Neither of them has any business being available in quantity.
recipes.lore_note: The salve made of thrift alone keeps a walker going. This keeps a walker going and lets them see where they are putting their feet, which up there is the half that matters.

discovery_milestones.title: The Pass, Under Glass
discovery_milestones.text: Every reagent in it grows an hour's climb above the valley and nowhere in it, and all of it came off a frame at the top of the tower. Rowan spent four years trying to carry the bell downhill and open it. The answer was that it was never a question of carrying it down.

recipes.name: Strandline Tonic
recipes.description: The whole shore in one bottle: something the water brought down, held in something the tower threw out.
recipes.lore_note: The glass is the interesting half. It came off these benches, so it takes a reaction the way the room expects one to be taken, which is why a shard off a window will not do.

recipes.name: Takehold Solution
recipes.description: Fern out of the bar shade held in water the house breathed out and caught again, drawn off cool so nothing in it is ever hurried.
recipes.lore_note: Both halves grew in a room where nothing arrives and nothing leaves. Brin's view is that this is exactly what a cutting needs for the first four days and exactly what would kill it on the fifth.

discovery_milestones.title: The House Grows Its Own
discovery_milestones.text: For two years the greenhouse has been a room with beds in it that you carry things up to. Nobody had walked the glass line, because there is no reason to walk between a bed and a wall unless you are looking for something, and nothing in the tower's books says anything grows there. Two things do, and neither of them has ever been outside. The house has been quietly running its own weather since before the sealing.
